$comment: The 100-point DGA compliance rubric. This file is the source of truth for the score — score.mjs reads it and does arithmetic, nothing more. Weights sum to 100 across 9 categories, 28 checks. Edit weights here to retune; never hand-adjust a score.
$gate: Government gate: any failed check with blocker:true caps the band at 'partial' regardless of the numeric score. The number is never altered — the band carries the gate, and the report names the blocker that capped it.
$passThreshold: How much compliance counts as a check being 'met' for the X-of-N headline. Ordinary checks pass at 90% — a couple of stray values on a large page is drift, not a failure. Blocker checks pass only at 100%, because WCAG conformance and mark usage are not proportional: one text run below 4.5:1 means the page does not conform, however good the other ninety-nine are.
$thresholds: Tolerances used by the auditor's matchers. deltaE is the CSS Color 4 deltaEOK — Euclidean distance in OKLab, scaled x100 — so 2.0 is about one just-noticeable difference: a designer cannot see a pass and can see a fail.

checks.title: Color token coverage
checks.description: Every text, background, border and fill color resolves to a DGA color token.
checks.measure: Occurrence-weighted share of color-bearing declarations within deltaE <= colorMatchDeltaE of some ledger color.
checks.fix: Replace the literal color with the named DGA token. The finding names the nearest token for each offender.

checks.title: No off-palette brand color
checks.description: No color far from every DGA token (deltaE > colorNearMissDeltaE) is used repeatedly as a brand or accent surface.
checks.measure: 1 minus the occurrence-weighted share of far-off-palette colors used at least offPaletteMinOccurrences times. Near-misses are C1's problem, not this one.
checks.fix: An unrecognisable brand color is an identity violation, not a styling preference. Move it onto the DGA palette or get the addition approved into the library.

checks.title: Semantic colors used semantically
checks.description: success / warning / error / info tokens appear only in their semantic roles, and those roles use no other color.
checks.measure: Share of semantic-token usages whose surrounding role matches the token's meaning, plus destructive/among-status affordances that use the correct token.
checks.fix: Error text in the brand green, or a success toast in red, breaks the one convention users carry between government platforms.

checks.title: Dark theme from the DS dark set
checks.description: If the target ships a dark theme, its colors come from the DGA dark-mode tokens rather than ad-hoc darkening.
checks.measure: Same coverage calculation as C1, run against the dark-scheme capture and the ledger's dark set.
checks.fix: Point the dark theme at the DGA dark tokens. Inverting or dimming light tokens drifts within one release.

checks.title: Typeface stack
checks.description: Latin and Arabic text render in the DGA typefaces, each script in the face specified for it.
checks.measure: Occurrence-weighted share of rendered text whose resolved font family is in the ledger's font stack for that script.
checks.fix: A substituted face is the single most visible compliance failure — it reads as a different government at a glance.

checks.title: Type scale
checks.description: Font sizes come from the DGA type ramp.
checks.measure: Occurrence-weighted share of computed font-size values matching a ramp step exactly (px, after rem resolution).
checks.fix: Snap to the nearest ramp step; the finding names it.

checks.title: Font weights
checks.description: Only the weights the DGA system defines are used.
checks.measure: Occurrence-weighted share of computed font-weight values in the ledger's allowed weight set.
checks.fix: Synthetic or off-scale weights render inconsistently across platforms, especially in Arabic.

checks.title: Line height and tracking
checks.description: Line-height and letter-spacing match the ramp step's paired values.
checks.measure: Share of text runs whose (size, line-height, letter-spacing) triple matches one ramp step. Matching leading alone lets a 14px body carry 72px display leading and pass, which is the mismatch this check exists to catch.
checks.fix: Set the ramp's paired leading rather than a global multiplier — Arabic ascenders and descenders need the extra room.

checks.title: Spacing scale
checks.description: Padding, margin and gap values sit on the DGA spacing grid.
checks.measure: Occurrence-weighted share of non-zero spacing values matching a scale step.
checks.fix: Off-grid spacing is what makes an otherwise on-token page feel unlike the rest of the platform.

checks.title: Container widths and gutters
checks.description: Page container max-widths, gutters and column behaviour follow the DGA breakpoints.
checks.measure: Measured at desktop, tablet and mobile captures; each breakpoint whose container width and gutter match the ledger scores its third.
checks.fix: Match the DGA container at each breakpoint so content lines up across linked government services.

checks.title: Vertical rhythm
checks.description: Section and block spacing uses the DGA rhythm steps rather than arbitrary gaps.
checks.measure: Share of between-section vertical gaps matching a rhythm step.
checks.fix: Use the rhythm steps for section separation; the page reads as one document rather than stacked fragments.

checks.title: Corner radii
checks.description: border-radius values come from the DGA radius scale.
checks.measure: Occurrence-weighted share of non-zero radii matching a scale step (fully-round pills excluded and checked against the pill token).
checks.fix: Snap to the nearest radius step.

checks.title: Borders
checks.description: Border widths and colors come from the DGA border tokens.
checks.measure: Share of visible borders whose width is on the scale and whose color is a ledger border token.
checks.fix: Use the border tokens; hairlines that vary by a fraction of a pixel show up as banding on scaled displays.

checks.title: Elevation
checks.description: box-shadow values come from the DGA elevation set.
checks.measure: Occurrence-weighted share of shadows matching an elevation token. Both sides are normalised to x/y/blur/spread plus rgba before comparison, because the ledger writes hex and the browser reports rgba() — comparing raw strings, or numbers scraped from them, can never match.
checks.fix: Use the named elevation level. Hand-tuned shadows break the depth ordering the system defines.

checks.title: DS components, not rebuilds
checks.description: Buttons, inputs, selects, cards, tabs, tables, navigation, modals and alerts correspond to DGA components rather than bespoke reimplementations.
checks.measure: Share of identified component instances matching a DGA component by anatomy. On Figma targets, whether the instance is a library instance rather than a detached or hand-drawn frame.
checks.fix: Adopt the library component. A rebuild that looks right today is the thing that drifts at the next DGA release.

checks.title: Variants, sizes and states
checks.description: Component variants (primary / secondary / tertiary), sizes and interaction states are the ones the system defines.
checks.measure: Share of instances whose variant, size and hover/active/disabled/focus treatments match the spec.
checks.fix: Missing disabled or focus treatments are the usual failure; both are specified, neither is optional.

checks.title: Component anatomy
checks.description: Internal padding, icon-and-label spacing and order, and minimum heights match the component spec.
checks.measure: Share of instances whose measured internal geometry matches the spec within 1px.
checks.fix: Restore the specified padding and min-height. Squeezed buttons are also the usual cause of an A4 target-size failure.

checks.title: Icon set
checks.description: Icons come from the DGA icon set, at scale sizes, with the specified stroke weight.
checks.measure: Share of icons identifiable as DGA set members at a scale size. Mixed icon libraries on one page fail proportionally.
checks.fix: Standardise on the DGA icon set. Two icon families on one screen is visible even to users who cannot name why.

checks.title: Logo and lockup
checks.description: Official marks use approved variants at or above minimum size, with the specified clear space, uncropped and unrecoloured.
checks.measure: Pass only if every mark on the target satisfies variant, minimum size, clear space and color rules.
checks.fix: Misuse of a government mark is an identity violation. Use the approved asset at approved size with its clear space intact.

checks.title: Direction and mirroring
checks.description: Arabic renders with dir=rtl and the layout mirrors — not just the text.
checks.measure: Correct dir/lang on the document and on mixed-script runs, plus evidence that layout order, alignment and navigation actually mirror in the RTL capture.
checks.fix: Set dir on the document and let logical properties carry the mirroring, rather than a per-component RTL override sheet.

checks.title: Logical properties
checks.description: Layout uses inline/block logical properties instead of left/right physical ones.
checks.measure: Share of directional declarations written logically rather than physically, in FIRST-PARTY stylesheets only. Vendor bundles are counted separately and reported as context — scoring them measures the framework choice rather than the team's work.
checks.fix: margin-inline-start over margin-left. Physical properties are why an RTL layout needs a second stylesheet and then diverges from the first.

checks.title: Arabic typography and numerals
checks.description: Arabic runs use the Arabic face, directional icons mirror, and the numeral system is consistent throughout.
checks.measure: Arabic-range text resolving to the Arabic face; chevrons and arrows mirrored in RTL; one numeral system (Arabic-Indic or Western) used consistently.
checks.fix: Mixed numeral systems inside one interface is the most common bilingual defect and the easiest to fix.

checks.title: Text contrast (WCAG AA)
checks.description: Every text run meets 4.5:1, or 3:1 where it qualifies as large text.
checks.measure: Occurrence-weighted share of text runs meeting their applicable threshold against their effective background.
checks.fix: Government services carry a statutory accessibility obligation. Darken the text token or lighten the surface — the finding gives the measured ratio and the needed delta.

checks.title: Non-text contrast
checks.description: UI boundaries, icons and graphical affordances meet 3:1 against their surroundings.
checks.measure: Share of borders that identify a UI COMPONENT or its state meeting 3:1 against their surroundings. Decorative borders — dividers, card outlines — are outside SC 1.4.11 and are skipped rather than failed; the skipped count is reported.
checks.fix: An input whose border disappears against its background is not usable at low vision or in sunlight.

checks.title: Visible focus
checks.description: Every interactive element shows a visible focus indicator on keyboard focus.
checks.measure: Share of a sample of focusable elements whose computed style changes while genuinely in :focus-visible — seeded via a throwaway text input, because el.focus() alone does not match the pseudo-class. Ring and colour-only indicators are tallied separately. The contrast of the indicator itself is not measured.
checks.fix: Never remove the outline without replacing it. Keyboard-only users navigate the whole service through this one affordance.

checks.title: Target size
checks.description: Interactive targets are at least 24x24 CSS px (WCAG 2.2 AA), spacing exceptions allowed.
checks.measure: Share of interactive elements meeting the minimum, with the WCAG 2.2 exceptions applied: a target inline in a sentence leaves the denominator, and an undersized target passes if a 24px circle centred on it intersects no other target. Both exemption counts are reported.
checks.fix: Grow the control or its padding. Icon-only buttons are the usual offenders.

checks.title: Motion tokens
checks.description: Transition durations and easing curves come from the DGA motion tokens.
checks.measure: Share of transition/animation declarations whose duration and timing function match motion tokens.
checks.fix: Use the named duration and curve so motion feels the same across services.

checks.title: Reduced motion
checks.description: prefers-reduced-motion is honoured.
checks.measure: Pass if the stylesheet carries a prefers-reduced-motion rule and animation is actually suppressed under the emulated preference.
checks.fix: Add a reduced-motion block that skips the motion rather than shortening it.

$parts: Categories roll up into the three parts DGA actually publishes, so a score can be read against the part of the system it belongs to. foundations is what the Foundations file defines; components is the Components Library plus Icons; standards is the RTL and accessibility guidance, which is not a library and is why it is a part of its own rather than being forced into one of the other two. Part scores are normalised to 100 within their own available weight so they are comparable to each other and to the overall.

parts.label: Foundations
parts.covers: Colour tokens, the type ramp, the spacing and radius scales, elevation and motion.

parts.label: Components
parts.covers: Component anatomy, variants and states, the icon set and official marks.

parts.label: Standards
parts.source: DGA guidance, not a Figma library
parts.covers: RTL and bilingual behaviour, and WCAG accessibility.
